title: Low-latency order book
summary: An order book on a nanosecond budget: contiguous levels with the best price at the back, O(1) cancel with stored list iterators, and what matters beyond big-O.

clips.title: Where the levels live
clips.question: In a nanosecond-budget order book, which container holds the price levels?

scenes.say: Low-latency order book, problem one. On a budget of tens of nanoseconds, which container should hold the price levels? Pause and answer out loud.

props.question: Which container holds the price levels, on a nanosecond budget?

scenes.say: Three options. A std map is sorted, with log n lookup, but every level is a separate heap node: pointer chasing, cache misses and allocations, around sixty to eighty nanoseconds. A sorted vector keeps the levels contiguous. Search it with lower bound, and since real books are shallow, inserting with memmove is cheap: around thirty nanoseconds. And if prices live in a small fixed range, index an array directly by tick: constant time everywhere, but memory for every possible price.

items.label: std::map
items.title: Tree of nodes
items.body: Sorted, O(log N), but pointer chasing and allocations.

items.label: std::vector
items.title: Contiguous
items.body: lower_bound + memmove; shallow books make it fast.

items.label: std::array
items.title: Direct index
items.body: (price − min) / tick: O(1), costly if sparse.

scenes.say: The vector trick is to reverse the sort. Bids sort ascending, so the best bid is at the back; asks sort descending, so the best ask is at the back too. Adding finds the level with lower bound, and usually it already exists, so we just add volume. And when the top level trades away, removing it is pop back: constant time, nothing shifts.

clips.title: O(1) cancel
clips.question: How do you cancel any order in O(1) while keeping FIFO order?

scenes.say: Problem two. Most messages are cancels. How do you cancel any order in constant time, while keeping first-in, first-out order at each price? Pause and answer out loud.

props.question: Cancel any order in O(1), keeping FIFO per price?

scenes.say: Use three structures. A sorted map of price levels, each holding a linked list of orders in arrival order, and a hash map from order ID to that order's list iterator. To cancel order two, look up its iterator in the hash map: constant time. Erase it from the list: its neighbours just relink, also constant time, and iterators to every other order stay valid. Subtract its volume from the level's cached total. Only when a level becomes empty do we touch the tree, in log n.

In code: the limit caches its total volume, and keeps its orders in a std list. The book adds the hash map from ID to iterator. Cancel looks up the iterator, finds its level, subtracts the volume, and erases the node, removing the level only if it is now empty.

highlights.note: Find the node, then its level
Unlink; drop the level only if empty

clips.title: Beyond big-O
clips.question: The algorithm is O(1). What else decides whether it runs in 50 nanoseconds?

scenes.say: Problem three. Your book is constant time on paper. What else decides whether it actually runs in fifty nanoseconds? Pause and answer out loud.

props.question: It's O(1) on paper. What else decides 50 ns?

scenes.say: Four things beyond big O. Never allocate on the hot path: preallocate orders and levels in an object pool. Search small books linearly, or with a branchless binary search, so the CPU never mispredicts. Keep rare paths, like a brand new price level, out of line and marked cold, so the hot loop stays in the instruction cache. And around the book, bypass the kernel for networking, and pass messages through lock-free shared memory ring buffers, with indices padded onto separate cache lines.

items.title: Zero allocation
items.body: Object pools for orders and levels.

items.label: Search
items.title: No mispredicts
items.body: Linear scan for small books, or branchless search.

items.label: Code layout
items.title: Cold paths out
items.body: New levels and errors go out of line.

items.label: I/O
items.title: Bypass + SPSC
items.body: Kernel bypass; padded lock-free ring buffers.

scenes.say: To recap. Keep levels contiguous, with the best price at the back. Store a list iterator per order ID, for constant-time cancel. Cache the volume per level. And on the hot path: no allocation, no avoidable branches, and no kernel.

items.text: Contiguous levels; best price at back().
Hot path: no allocation, branches, or kernel.
